name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R+22 partisan lean of the district
Incumbent Mike Bost running with a large financial edge ($790K vs $60K cash)
No polls or expert ratings; challenger is lightly funded
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Bost's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage leave Fortier with no visible path, and markets price her win odds at just 3%. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays at a roughly 19-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Bost underperforming his lean, or significant outside spending against him, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Bost seeks another term in a southern Illinois district that leans heavily Republican, about 22 points toward the GOP at the baseline. He is a well-established incumbent with roughly $790,000 on hand after raising more than $1.3 million. Democrat Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000 with about $60,000 cash, and no outside groups have entered the race on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which give Bost roughly a 97% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe R.
